articles.headlineTranslated: Measles infection in a man in his 30s; returned from Europe at the end of last month; city calls on fellow passengers on the same flight to take precautions; Toyama City, Toyama Prefecture (published July 3, 2026) | KNB NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Measles confirmed in a man in his 30s in Toyama City, Toyama Prefecture, bringing the prefecture’s total to eight cases since last month. The patient returned from Europe on June 30, traveling from Haneda Airport to Toyama Airport on an All Nippon Airways flight departing at 16:20, and developed fever the day after return. Laboratory confirmation by the prefectural health laboratory was announced today; he is currently undergoing home treatment. He had visited Italy and Spain during Europe travel, where measles is circulating, and authorities consider Europe to be the most likely source. Because the flight carries airborne transmission risk, fellow passengers on the June 30 ANA flight are urged to monitor their health for the next three weeks. If fever or rash appears, avoid going out and contact a medical facility in advance, following physician instructions.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles outbreak warning: seven cases in three weeks — "Get vaccinated"
articles.summary: Seven measles cases have been confirmed in Toyama Prefecture over roughly three weeks since a mid-June resurgence began. The index case is a man in his 20s with travel history to Indonesia; he developed fever and rash, and four close contacts were subsequently infected. Two additional cases with travel history but no known contact were also identified. Measles is highly contagious and spreads by droplets and airborne transmission; in unimmunized individuals infection is nearly universal. Incubation is 10–12 days; initial symptoms include fever, cough, runny nose, followed by fever and rash. Pneumonia and other complications can occur. Nationwide, 539 cases were reported as of June 21, with Tokyo accounting for 262. Vaccination remains the most effective defense: two-dose schedule (ages 1 and 5–7); Toyama’s 2024 first-dose 91.8% and second-dose 93.5%. Verify vaccination history and vaccinate if incomplete; suspected cases should contact the nearest public health center and seek medical care.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles spread even within Toyama Prefecture: what to watch out for (Posted July 2, 2026) | KNB NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Measles is spreading in Japan, with Toyama Prefecture reporting seven confirmed cases in the Takaoka Public Health Center area, after the first case appeared last month. Nationally, measles cases exceed 500, well above last year’s total. Dr. Kazunori Oishi, director of the Toyama Prefectural Institute of Public Health, says measles is highly contagious and presents with fever, mucosal symptoms, respiratory symptoms, and rash. Transmission occurs by droplets, contact, and airborne routes; exposure in the same space can infect those without immunity. Vaccination with the measles–mumps–rubella (MR) vaccine remains the best defense. Most cases have one or two doses, but protection can wane about ten years after vaccination, so breakthrough infections occur. If only one dose is on record, an additional dose may be considered. Suspected cases should call ahead to medical facilities before visiting, and those under 40 may have lower antibody levels and should be vigilant.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles: Governor Issues Warning, Urges Vaccination
articles.summary: Measles infections are being reported in Toyama Prefecture, prompting Governor Hachiro Nitta to urge vaccination at a July 2, 2026 press conference. While the governor notes that about 95% of residents reportedly have measles antibodies and cautions against excessive fear, he emphasizes that infants remain at higher risk of severe outcomes such as pneumonia and encephalitis, and that family members should receive additional vaccination. Individuals planning overseas travel and airport personnel are advised to be vigilant. Japan’s routine measles immunization consists of two doses: first at age one and a second before entering elementary school; beyond these, vaccination is voluntary and paid. The prefecture’s official website lists medical facilities where vaccines are available, facilitating access for residents and travelers alike.

articles.headlineTranslated: Japan-developed Nipah virus vaccine for a high-fatality Nipah virus begins clinical trials in Belgium
articles.summary: Japan-developed Nipah virus vaccine, using a live-attenuated measles virus vector carrying Nipah genes, began clinical trials in Belgium on June 15, testing safety and immunogenicity in 60 healthy adults. Nipah virus, transmitted from fruit bats to people (and occasionally via human contact), can cause fever and myalgia and may progress to encephalitis with high fatality; there are no approved treatments or vaccines. The vaccine showed safety and efficacy in animal studies. If safety and immune response are confirmed, trials are planned in Bangladesh, where Nipah outbreaks occur. The project is led by Misako Yoneda of Teikyo University, with collaborators including the European Vaccine Initiative, Stanford University, and Japan’s Center for Advanced Research and Development Strategy. Researchers describe this as a potential step toward a practical vaccine against a deadly, zoonotic infection.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles spreading in the Tokyo metropolitan area and urban Kansai areas: a quick refresher on what kind of disease it is.
articles.summary: Measles is spreading in the Tokyo metropolitan area and urban Kansai areas, likely surpassing the 2019 peak. Those in their late teens to 30s form the outbreak core, with immunity lower among this group than among 50s+ who had natural exposure, making measles a concern for young adults as well as children. After a 10–12 day incubation, patients develop fever (~38°C), cough, runny nose, and conjunctivitis; the catarrhal stage is the most contagious, with transmission risk near 100% for susceptible contacts and possible infection after a 30-minute room exposure. A subsequent fever spike (≥39°C) accompanies a characteristic red rash that starts on the neck or forehead and spreads to the body; pneumonia and encephalitis risk rise. Contagiousness persists for three days after fever subsides. Vaccination is the most reliable prevention: one dose is >95% effective; two doses are recommended. If immunity history is unknown, check with a blood test.
articles.summaryOriginal: Measles is spreading in the Tokyo metropolitan area and urban Kansai areas, likely surpassing the 2019 peak. Those in their late teens to 30s form the outbreak core, with immunity lower among this group than among 50s+ who had natural exposure, making measles a concern for young adults as well as children. After a 10–12 day incubation, patients develop fever (~38°C), cough, runny nose, and conjunctivitis; the catarrhal stage is the most contagious, with transmission risk near 100% for susceptible contacts and possible infection after a 30-minute room exposure. A subsequent fever spike (≥39°C) accompanies a characteristic red rash that starts on the neck or forehead and spreads to the body; pneumonia and encephalitis risk rise. Contagiousness persists for three days after fever subsides. Vaccination is the most reliable prevention: one dose is >95% effective; two doses are recommended. If immunity history is unknown, check with a blood test.

articles.headline: 今年の「はしか」患者数525人に　今月7日までの1週間で全国で新たに2人確認（2026年6月16日掲載）｜日テレNEWS NNN
articles.headlineTranslated: Measles cases this year reach 525; two new nationwide cases confirmed in the week through the 7th of this month (Published June 16, 2026) | Nippon TV News NNN
articles.summary: Measles cases in Japan this year reach 525, with two new nationwide infections reported in the week through June 7 (one in Chiba Prefecture and one in Gunma Prefecture). The cumulative total is about 3.9 times higher than the same period last year. Dr. Takeshi Terashima, a respiratory medicine specialist, notes measles spreads more easily at around 20°C, suggesting seasonal factors may slow the current rise. Nonetheless, infections commonly peak from spring to early summer, and increased international travel during summer vacations could boost case numbers. The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare urges travelers to consider vaccination as appropriate before overseas trips.
